newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - N.Ireland seeks cost savings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - N.Ireland seeks cost savings.

text.p: Regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Ireland Electricity (NIE) will seek cost savings whatever the outcome of a review of prices by UK competition authorities, chief executive Patrick Haren said.
"No matter what the outcome, we will be looking for new efficiency gains," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Haren said the company was hoping for "a reasonably fair outcome to give an incentive to continue driving the company to efficiencies."
NIE's dispute with its regulator Ofreg over a pricing review is being considered by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), which should report by March 17.
Haren said the company wanted an indication from regulators on whether it should continue planned levels of investment.
"The regulator in his price proposals signalled his view that we should not maintain those levels," he said.
NIE had planned to spend 400 million stg over the next five years on infrastructure and other investments, he said.
NIE turned in pretax profits of 52 million stg for the half year, up from 47.7 million stg previously and paid an interim dividend of 5.5 pence compared with five pence.
Haren said the company had "maintained good progress on the dividend."
He said underlying sales were up around 2.9 percent, reflecting "a strong sales performance in our system."
"It is a fairly steady set of results, no particular news, no surprises or disappointments," he said.
